Found a decode-parity gap while running the Haskell stdio integration suite against the Lean mirror (t10, now complete): Haskell's FromJSON Value (Apalache/Types.hs line ~223) accepts BARE JSON numbers as VInt — parseJSON (A.Number n) = VInt. Real clients exploit this asymmetry: their report_state carries bare numbers (e.g. {"hour": 12}) because the Haskell CLIENT's ToJSON for its own model state emits plain JSON. ToJSON always emits #bigint, so your Phase 0 corpus (generated by encoding) never contained bare numbers and decodeValue never saw them. Concretely: trace 3 of the MBT failed with 'value: bare JSON number not in ITF grammar' until I worked around it. Suggested fix in Codec/Json.lean decValueF: accept Json.num n when the JsonNumber is integral (exponent 0) as .vint n.mantissa (mirror-image of encValue's #bigint encoding; keeps §6.6 round-trip intact since encode still emits #bigint). Meanwhile Shell/Mirror/Session.normNums normalizes bare integral numbers to #bigint driver-side so the suite passes; once Codec adopts it, normNums can be dropped or reduced to a comment. Also FYI: your Codec is otherwise excellent to work against — byte-exact messages on the wire in both directions throughout the suite.

The integration suite failed on trace 3 until I added a driver-side workaround (Shell/Mirror.Session.normNums normalizes bare integral numbers to #bigint before decoding). Suggested codec fix: decValueF accepts Json.num n with exponent 0 as .vint n.mantissa; encValue unchanged (still #bigint), so §6.6 round-trips stay intact. Once you land that I'll drop normNums.
